Geometric metrics:
  Every successful 'agentcad run' returns a 'metrics' key with:

  bounding_box   {x: [min,max], y: [min,max], z: [min,max]}
  dimensions     {x: float, y: float, z: float}  (bbox extents)
  volume         float (mm^3)
  surface_area   float (mm^2)
  center_of_mass {x, y, z}
  face_count     int
  edge_count     int
  is_valid       bool or null: the deliverable verdict (kernel check,
                 closed shells, manifold mesh); see 'agentcad docs
                 validation'. null means a layer could not finish.
  reliable       bool: false when the shape has no solid or an open
                 shell, so volume and surface_area are not physical

  Metrics are also saved in meta.json and compared by 'agentcad diff'.
  Use metrics to verify shape correctness without rendering.

  Units: agentcad is unit-agnostic. All dimensions, volume, and area
  are reported in whatever units your script uses. Scripts default to
  millimeters (the OpenCascade convention), so volume is mm^3 and area
  is mm^2 unless you chose a different convention in your script.

Geometry validation (is_valid):
  Every command that reports geometry (run, import, inspect, measure,
  check-spec, recover) runs the same layered validator and reports one
  verdict in metrics.is_valid (inspect: top-level is_valid):
    true   every gating layer passed; the part is deliverable
    false  a gating layer failed; validation.first_failure names it
    null   a gating layer could not finish (timeout); see
           validation.undetermined_layer and the warnings list

  Layers, in order (validation.layers.<name>.status):
    file_parse     the file could be read as CAD
    kernel_load    the kernel produced a non-empty shape
    brep_check     the kernel consistency check (what is_valid meant
                   before 0.6); errors lists BRepCheck classes;
                   entities locates failing faces/edges/vertices by ID
    shell_closure  every shell closed, no loose faces; free_edge_ids
                   and free_edges (with endpoints) locate any gap
    mesh_manifold  the tessellation is a closed orientable manifold;
                   defect gives kind, location, and face_ids
    structure      solid/shell/face counts; gates when expectations are declared
    advisory       sliver faces, loose tolerances (reports, never gates)

  A closed box passes every layer. A box with one face removed is
  kernel-consistent (brep_check pass) but fails shell_closure with four
  free edges, so is_valid is false and run records the attempt as
  invalid_geometry without exporting a STEP. metrics.reliable is false
  when there is no solid or an open shell: the reported volume is not a
  physical quantity then.

  Locate and repair failures on an existing STEP:
    agentcad inspect part.step --ids
    agentcad render part.step --view iso --highlight validation
    agentcad view part.step --validation
  Red markers show reported edges and vertices in context. Evidence IDs
  match inspect --ids on the same file; they can change after edits.
  Mesh defects without a corresponding B-rep edge/vertex have empty ID
  lists and retain coordinates and adjacent face_ids. Evidence is capped;
  evidence_truncated says when additional failures were omitted.
  For geometry failures, validation.guidance separates the measured
  finding, what remains unknown, and next_checks. The suggestion field
  gives these inspection steps, not an assumed repair. An open shell
  does not prove a missing face or disconnected coincident boundaries.
  validation.repairs contains possible options, all with applicability:
  unverified. Each links evidence (layer and measured message), explains
  a possible cause in why, and requires a precondition before using how.
  Related evidence does not prove that a repair applies. changes_intent:
  false describes intended preservation under that condition, not a
  safety verdict. Sewing existing faces cannot fill a missing face.
  The viewer collapses these options under Possible repairs (unverified).
  No repairs are applied automatically. Review the intended design
  before changing geometry; revalidate the exported STEP after edits.

  Structure expectations (non-negative integer counts):
    show_object(part, options={"expect_solids": 1, "expect_shells": 1})
  Each declaration applies to that show_object result, after STEP
  round-trip. A mismatch fails structure, including under kernel profile.
  check-spec also accepts {"expect_solids": 1} without a features array;
  those expectations apply to the whole file. It reports passed: false
  and is_valid: false on a mismatch (the check command still succeeds).
  Counts are invocation-specific; inspecting the file without the
  expectation reports its geometric deliverability again.
  Named parts have parts[].connection: nearest part, distance_mm, and
  status. Separation above 0.01 mm warns but never gates a run. Set
  options={"floating": True} for intentional separation. A single
  named part has no neighbor and reports not_applicable.

  The verdict is computed on the artifact that ships: run exports the
  STEP first and validates the reloaded file, so run, inspect, and
  measure agree on the same output.step. Export can change topology
  (two bodies fused along a shared edge become two clean bodies in the
  file), which is why the file, not the in-memory shape, is judged.
  run also records validation.step_round_trip: before/after layer
  outcomes and solid counts, matches (true/false/null), and differences.
  This comparison is diagnostic, not an additional gate: two invalid
  shapes can match, and STEP normalization can change a failure into a
  pass. Only the reloaded artifact controls the existing run gate.
  Above 500 faces the kernel check and tessellation are not repeated on
  the in-memory source; step_round_trip.skipped_layers names them and
  the reloaded STEP still runs every layer.
  See docs export for separate checks of the written mesh bytes.

  Profiles (--validation-profile on run, import, inspect):
    deliverable  default; gates on brep_check, shell_closure, and
                 mesh_manifold
    kernel       the pre-0.6 contract: brep_check alone gates; the
                 other layers are reported as skipped. Use it for
                 intentional surfaces or sheet bodies. The profile
                 used is recorded as validation_profile in the
                 response and meta.json. The profile is per
                 invocation: measure, check-spec, and inspect on an
                 exported STEP evaluate deliverable unless you pass
                 --validation-profile again (measure and check-spec
                 have no flag), so a kernel-profile version reports
                 is_valid: false when re-inspected. That is expected
                 for a sheet body.

  Per-part metrics (parts[].metrics.is_valid) remain the kernel check
  only, so a part can read true inside an invalid_geometry response;
  the top-level metrics.is_valid is the verdict to act on.
  The mesh layer runs in a bounded subprocess
  (AGENTCAD_MESH_VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_S, default 60).
  Written files of 1 MB or more (run's exported STEP, import's source)
  validate in a worker process under AGENTCAD_VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_S
  (default 120; 0 disables). On timeout every finished layer is kept,
  the running layer is 'timeout', later layers are 'skipped', and
  is_valid is null unless a gating layer already failed. The report
  carries worker, budget_s, and timed_out_layer.
  When a run's result is invalid and the script loaded a file with
  load_step()/load_step_shape(), run validates each loaded input too:
  validation.inherited_from_input names the input whose own first
  failure is the same layer (the run did not introduce it), or is
  false when every input passes that layer (the run introduced it).
  validation.inputs_checked lists each input's verdict. Repair the
  input, not the edit, when the failure is inherited.

Pre-execution static checks (status validation_error, timings.validation_ms):
  Before building geometry, 'agentcad run' performs fast static checks.
  Failures return immediately (<100ms) with status 'validation_error',
  without consuming a version number or creating disk artifacts.

  Checks:
    syntax_error        Python syntax validation (ast.parse)
    show_object_missing Script must call show_object() to surface geometry
    import_error        All imported modules must be resolvable

  Missing output capture is checked before CAD imports or daemon routing.
  Its check includes candidate variables and copyable repair_snippets,
  e.g. show_object(plate). With multiple candidates, choose the intended
  output explicitly; agentcad never selects a shape automatically.
  Call entry points at module scope: an if __name__ == '__main__' guard
  does not run in agentcad. Skipped entry points get a repair snippet.
  A capture skipped dynamically still fails at execution with a repair.

  Output format:
    {"command": "run", "status": "validation_error",
     "checks": [{"check": "...", "severity": "error", "message": "..."}],
     "message": "No STEP was created. Fix script.py and rerun the command.",
     "artifact_created": false, "outputs": {"step": null},
     "next_actions": ["agentcad run script.py --label fixed"]}

Live project viewer:
  Normal run/import commands open a stable local project URL. Share
  project_viewer.url with the human and leave the tab open: completed
  builds refresh automatically, preserving camera and compatible review
  state. viewer remains the immutable per-version HTML snapshot.
  The live page keeps the last successful model after a failed build.
  New models load fully before replacing the displayed model.

  agentcad viewer          # open or reuse the current project
  agentcad viewer status   # inspect the lightweight local service
  agentcad viewer stop     # stop it; retain the port and URLs
  agentcad viewer open     # restart if needed and open the project

  --no-view never opens a browser or starts this service. When it still
  generates viewer assets, an existing page receives those builds. The
  core-only --no-preview --no-diff --no-view path generates no viewer;
  the page retains its prior model and reports preview unavailable.

  Updates are polled once a second, less frequently in background tabs.
  Browser clients expire after 90 seconds without a heartbeat; a sleeping
  tab may be considered disconnected and a later run can open another.
  Closing/navigating away releases the lease when the browser delivers
  its pagehide event. After a forced close, use the saved URL directly
  or wait for the lease to expire before automatic reopening.
  The service binds only to 127.0.0.1 and serves registered snapshots
  through private project URLs. These links work only on this machine.
  Moving the project changes its URL; renaming a build does not.
  State: ~/.cache/agentcad/viewer (AGENTCAD_VIEWER_HOME overrides it).
  With a configured build root, state instead lives in its .agentcad/viewer
  directory; this takes precedence over AGENTCAD_VIEWER_HOME.
  Preserve this directory to keep URLs stable. If the saved port is
  occupied, free it and retry; AgentCAD never kills another listener.
  For incompatible protocol versions, stop the service using the
  installation that started it before opening with the new one.
  If service startup fails, the CAD build and version snapshot remain
  usable; project_viewer reports unavailable with a diagnostic message.

=== Deliver ===
Exporting mesh formats:
  agentcad export <step_file> --format stl,glb,obj
  agentcad run script.py --label label --export stl,glb,obj

  Supported formats: stl, glb, obj
  Files are written alongside the STEP file.
  In a version directory, meta.json outputs are updated.
  status: success means files were written, not that every mesh passed.
  export reports the source CAD validation and is_valid separately from
  mesh_validation.stl/glb/obj, computed by reopening each written file.
  Each mesh report includes is_valid, triangle_count, watertight,
  manifold, file_parse/mesh_manifold layers, checked_file, and sha256.
  run --export also returns and persists mesh_validation in meta.json.
  Failed or undetermined mesh checks warn and retain the files; they
  do not invalidate a successful STEP version or move current back.
  Before handing off a mesh, require its own is_valid: true.
  Checks have a 30-second per-file budget, 128 MiB byte limit, and
  one-million-triangle limit. A timeout/error is unknown (null), not
  invalid; completed layers are retained. Malformed bytes fail parsing.
  Only exactly equal positions are joined. GLB scene nodes stay
  separate; STL/OBJ lose body identity, so touching bodies can become
  non-manifold there despite valid source CAD. No faces are repaired,
  removed, or retessellated by the check. Self-intersections, units,
  dimensions, printability, and faithful shape reproduction are not
  certified. 3MF and general mesh import are not implemented.

  In scripts, you can also import directly:
    from agentcad.export import export_glb
    export_glb(shape, 'output.glb')  # shape must be a TopoDS_Shape

  GLB export auto-colors individual solids — each part gets a distinct
  color from a built-in palette for easy identification in 3D viewers.
  GLB export handles tessellation automatically — use `agentcad export`
  or export_glb() for GLTF/GLB; script-level mesh exporters are not
  supported.

Artifact directories and version labels:
  Default: agentcad.json, .agentcad state, and vN_LABEL versions live
  at the project root, just as in existing projects.

  Persistent setting: create agentcad.toml in the source project:
    build_dir = "./build"
  Then run agentcad init. This creates build/agentcad.json.
  Scripts, edit.py, and installed agent guidance stay in the source
  project. Generated geometry, metadata, viewers, logs, and feedback
  bundles live below the selected build directory.

  One-command override (does not edit agentcad.toml):
    agentcad init --build-dir /tmp/cad-build
    agentcad run model.py --label first --build-dir /tmp/cad-build
    agentcad context --build-dir /tmp/cad-build
    agentcad parts --build-dir /tmp/cad-build list current
    agentcad recover v1_first --build-dir /tmp/cad-build

  Precedence: --build-dir > agentcad.toml build_dir > project root.
  Relative build directories resolve from the nearest project root
  (agentcad.toml or legacy agentcad.json), even from a subdirectory.
  Without a marker, the invocation directory is the project root.
  An empty agentcad.toml can anchor projects using only overrides.
  Explicit input filenames still resolve from the invocation directory.
  Each build root has independent history; initialize it explicitly.
  Changing the setting never moves or merges old history.
  No environment-variable interpolation occurs inside TOML.

  JSON reports project_root, build_root, and build_root_source.
  Root source is command, project_config, default, or manifest when
  discovering a configured build from inside its generated tree.
  Configured artifacts are returned as absolute paths; default paths
  retain their existing project-relative strings when invoked at root.
  Always use returned outputs.step, viewer, and renders paths.
  On-disk manifest/meta paths remain relative to the build root.
  Standalone render/export/view of outside inputs writes under
  build_root/derived, with distinct directories for same-named inputs.
  --label names a version; deprecated --output never means a path.
  Configured live-viewer service state lives in build_root/.agentcad/viewer.
  Each build root has its own service and live URL; viewer open/status/stop
  accept --build-dir. Default projects retain the shared user service.

Retained change attempts (local CLI and MCP):
  Initialized run/import histories return change with a revision_id,
  parent_revision_id, and absolute source/candidate/receipt/diagnostics
  paths under build_root/.agentcad/changes/attempts. Read those JSON
  records with ordinary file tools; retained artifacts are hash-checked.
  Source is saved before execution/loading. Failed syntax, execution,
  malformed imports, and invalid geometry remain addressable without
  replacing the last successful current version. Interrupted attempts
  remain in_progress; they are not silently called successful.
  A request.json without outcome.json identifies an unfinished attempt.
  change.status=incomplete reports a retention failure; inspect its
  request and warning. If final diagnostics fail after acceptance, the
  successful CAD result/current stays accepted. unavailable means the
  attempt could not be retained; do not assume its evidence was saved.
  change.geometry may hold diagnostic STEP bytes even when
  outputs.step is null. It is not an accepted deliverable. Optional
  declared outputs (including geometry manifests) are retained separately
  in the diagnostics record, with unavailable artifacts listed explicitly.
  Never edit retained files in place: copy source to a working script,
  repair it, and run again to create a successor. Existing version
  numbers/current behavior is unchanged; this adds no promote command.
  This preserves entry source and emitted artifacts, not arbitrary Python
  dependencies or the entire execution environment. Dry runs do not
  create retained attempts, and uninitialized projects are not adopted.

=== Setup, recovery, and reference ===
Installation:
  Requires Python 3.10-3.12 (OpenCascade bindings do not support 3.13+).

  pip install agentcad

  This installs agentcad and everything the default build123d runtime
  needs (build123d, the OpenCascade binding, Click). No separate
  package installation is needed.

  Optional extras:
    pip install "agentcad[mcp]"       # MCP server for native agent tools
    pip install "agentcad[cadquery]"  # CadQuery compatibility runtime

  CadQuery is NOT included by default. The cadquery extra adds CadQuery
  and its own dependency chain (CasADi plus bundled COIN-OR solver
  libraries), a larger third-party license surface than the default
  install. Only add it for existing CadQuery scripts or projects.

  After installing, the 'agentcad' command is available in your shell.
  Run 'agentcad docs' to see full documentation.

agentcad commands by required workflow stage:

  Inspect
  context — Show project state and interrupted version recovery candidates.
  inspect — Inspect STEP/BREP topology, orientation, IDs, risk, and
            validation evidence. --ids is capped by default; use
            --no-limit explicitly.
  measure — Measure overall dimensions and feature sizes in STEP/BREP files.
            Full feature output is capped by default; use --no-limit explicitly.
  render  — Render PNG views of an existing STEP file.
  parts   — List/show parts captured for a version snapshot, or generate
            part review viewers with hide/isolate/ghost/focus state.

  Specify
  Write requirements before building. check-spec consumes an explicit
  JSON geometry contract during Validate.

  Build
  run     — Execute a build123d script (or explicit CadQuery compatibility
            script), producing versioned STEP output.
            Use --label to name the version; the artifact path is returned
            in outputs.step. --output is a deprecated alias for --label
            and never denotes a destination path. --label is optional
            with --dry-run, which writes nothing.
            Pass an existing .py script; shell scripts are rejected.
            --runtime selects build123d or cadquery, not python; omit it
            to follow the project runtime. --export accepts stl, glb, obj.
            STEP is always produced by a successful build; use outputs.step
            without --export step. Input errors include next_actions.
            Normally produces: STEP, GLB, viewer.html, and (from v2) diff PNGs.
            Opens or reuses project_viewer.url; --no-view opts out. From v2,
            the viewer preloads A=previous and B=current for comparison.
            Options: --render, --export, --no-preview (skips preview PNGs),
                     --no-diff (skips automatic comparison; agentcad diff
                     remains available), --no-view (skips browser launch).
            Core-only fast path: --no-preview --no-diff --no-view writes
            output.step, script.py, meta.json (including metrics), and only
            explicitly requested exports.
  import  — Adopt STEP/STP/BREP as a version; --no-diff skips automatic
            comparison without disabling an explicit agentcad diff.

  Validate
  check-spec
          — Compare measured cylindrical features against an explicit JSON spec.
  review  — Participate in shared spatial comment threads.
  diff    — Compare two versions of a model.
            Exact comparison has a 30s default worker budget; set
            AGENTCAD_DIFF_TIMEOUT_S=N to override it (0 disables it).
            Exact failure automatically runs a bounded approximate voxel
            comparison; set AGENTCAD_APPROX_DIFF_TIMEOUT_S to tune its budget.
  view    — Open one GLB/STEP model, or two models as synchronized A/B.
            Pass --overlay to start a two-model review in tinted overlay mode.
            Use --measure or --spec spec.json for read-only measurement review.

  Deliver
  export  — Export a validated STEP file to mesh formats (STL, GLB, OBJ);
            check the returned per-format mesh validation before handoff.
  viewer  — Open the stable live project (default), or inspect/stop its
            local service: agentcad viewer [open|status|stop].

  Setup, recovery, and reference
  cloud   — Use hosted projects via explicit cloud operations; see docs cloud.
  init    — Initialize a new agentcad project (creates agentcad.json).
  recover — Validate and reconcile one interrupted version directory.
  docs    — Show this documentation.
  feedback
          — Send an observation to the agentcad team (any friction,
            any time — bundles your session log automatically).

Artifact locations: use returned paths. To separate generated files
from source with agentcad.toml or --build-dir, see `agentcad docs artifacts`.

Response schema:
  All commands return JSON with 'command' and 'status' fields.

  Streams:
    stdout carries the JSON response — parse this.
    stderr carries human-readable progress/diagnostics — not JSON.
    Do NOT merge the streams with '2>&1' before a JSON parser, or the
    progress lines will corrupt the parse. If you must capture both,
    redirect them to separate destinations.

  Status values:
    success — The command's primary work completed. Inspect artifact status
              for optional post-processing details.
    failed  — A script execution failed (e.g. geometry error, no show_object).
              Includes 'error' with details. Targeted recoveries also include
              'suggestion' and 'more_at'. No STEP is created; message and
              next_actions tell the agent to fix and rerun the script. A
              diagnostic version directory is created.
    error   — A CLI-level error (missing file, bad arguments, no manifest).
              Includes 'message'. Initialized readable change attempts
              may retain diagnostics under change; no accepted CAD output.
    validation_error — A static script check failed. No numbered version
              is created; change retains the source unless --dry-run.
              The response includes a directly
              executable fix-and-rerun command in next_actions.
    invalid_geometry — Source execution/loading and metrics completed, but
              the final shape is not deliverable under the validation
              profile (default: kernel check, closed shells, manifold
              mesh). first_failure names the layer and validation holds
              the evidence. Diagnostic metadata and the source are
              recorded as a numbered history entry unless --dry-run; no
              accepted STEP is exported and current does not advance.
              change.geometry may retain diagnostic bytes. Check
              version_recorded and current_advanced in the response.
    validation_timeout — Inspect exceeded its validation budget. The file
              is not classified as malformed; timed_out_phase, elapsed_s,
              validation_phases, retryable, and next_actions identify a
              structural-only or larger-budget retry.
    CAD file readers may also return non-success diagnostic statuses:
              empty, malformed, unknown_format, display_format,
              recognized_deferred, or limited. These include message and/or
              suggestion fields plus detected file metadata when available.
    malformed CAD uses error_kind=malformed_cad and one executable
              next_actions recovery. Never repair STEP by writing or
              truncating text; use a kernel-backed run or valid import.
    Click usage failures use status=error with stable error_kind, message,
              usage, invalid_option, and next_actions fields on stdout.
              For `run`, next_actions[0] is a corrected command: the script,
              label, and other options that parsed, with SCRIPT or LABEL
              standing in for what did not. canonical_command is
              `agentcad run SCRIPT --label LABEL`. A script path that does
              not exist returns error_kind=script_not_found and one run
              command per Python script in the directory.
              Missing paths, non-file inputs, and non-Python scripts (such
              as .sh) are rejected before daemon routing. CAD file inputs
              still dispatch to import. --runtime selects build123d or
              cadquery, not python; omit it to follow the project runtime.
              --export accepts mesh formats stl, glb, obj. STEP is always
              produced by a successful build: read outputs.step, without
              --export step. Invalid formats return a corrected command.
              --label remains required for builds (e.g. --label first),
              and optional with --dry-run. For missing output paths in
              render/export, next_actions retries with the current
              successful version's recorded outputs.step when available,
              preserving command options and the selected build directory.
              For these CLI input-error recoveries, next_actions contains
              commands or SCRIPT/LABEL templates; prose belongs in suggestion.
              Successful init/context guidance may include explanations
              after ' — '; execute only the command before that separator.

  Artifact key convention (used everywhere — command output, meta.json, diff):
    outputs — dict of explicit 3D model artifacts. Keys: step, script,
              stl, glb, obj. outputs.glb appears only when --export glb
              was requested; viewer_glb normally backs viewer.html and is
              skipped by the core-only fast path.
    renders — dict of 2D PNG renders. Keys: view name (iso, front, top, ...) or
              custom angle key ('45_30') or --name override.
    Both are present when populated; commands that only produce one kind only
    return that key. Do NOT look for 'renders' inside 'outputs' or vice versa.
    run always returns label, artifact_created, and outputs.step; when no
              STEP was created, artifact_created=false and outputs.step=null.
    run stdout is exactly one JSON document. Everything the script writes
              to stdout (print, os.write(1, ...), child processes) is
              returned as script_output (about the last 4000 chars; key
              omitted when nothing was written), on success and failure.
              Writes to sys.stderr pass through to stderr.
    change    Retained attempt references for initialized local run/import
              operations. Read docs artifacts for scope and recovery.
              completed means the response was retained, not that checks
              passed; read the receipt validation_state and blockers.
    core      Core CAD lifecycle. status=success means metrics, validity, and
              STEP export completed and the version is already registered.
    artifacts Optional post-processing groups. Each reports pending, success,
              unavailable, timeout, failed, or skipped. Artifact failure does
              not reverse core success or remove the registered STEP. Keep and
              use that STEP; retry only optional render/view work if needed.
    comparison_phases
              Observable comparison stages shared by run/import automatic
              diff, explicit diff, and two-model view. Each attempted stage
              has status plus duration_ms; skipped stages have an explanatory
              message and no duration. comparison_phases is omitted when no
              comparison was attempted (for example, the first project run).
              Read the largest duration_ms to find the most expensive
              stage without treating every delay as one opaque diff. Ordered keys:
                source_loading
                comparison_rendering
                projection_comparison
                exact_3d_comparison
                approximate_3d_comparison
                difference_artifact_export
                viewer_generation
              Source panels are captured once during comparison_rendering;
              projection_comparison reuses those pixels instead of rendering
              either model again. Projection silhouettes use a segmentation
              background independent of display material and lighting.
              Projection scores describe visual overlap across the four
              views; they do not prove physical correctness or shared volume.
              Exact 3D comparison runs in a terminable worker with a 30s
              default budget. AGENTCAD_DIFF_TIMEOUT_S=N overrides it; 0
              disables the dedicated limit for diagnostics. A timeout affects
              only exact_3d_comparison and preserves projection and the
              committed version. It then starts a bounded voxel fallback.
              Successful fallback responses use method=approximate_voxel_volume,
              report resolution_mm plus a non-strict error_estimate whose
              absolute_volume values are heuristic errors (not measurements),
              and keep
              the original diagnostics under comparison_3d.exact_attempt.
              AGENTCAD_APPROX_DIFF_TIMEOUT_S controls its 30s worker budget;
              AGENTCAD_APPROX_RESOLUTION_MM requests a grid resolution, which
              may be coarsened to cap sampled cells. Exact comparison uses
              independent geometry copies and one non-destructive exact
              partition. Native diagnostics appear at comparison_3d.kernel
              for exact results and comparison_3d.exact_attempt.kernel after
              fallback; exact_partition_runs disambiguates the
              exact pass from compound canonicalization, and repeated native
              messages include counts instead of duplicate entries.
              Unavailable results include a suggestion. comparison_3d
              volume_semantics explains compound overlap only when an input
              actually required occupied-volume canonicalization.
              Impossible or non-conserving volumes are never published.
              If exact volumes are still
              needed, run agentcad diff OLD NEW with a larger budget; do not
              rerun the original run/import and create a duplicate version.

  Per-command response fields (on status='success'):
    init     project, runtime?
    run      core, artifacts, runtime, output_type, version, label,
             artifact_created, outputs (outputs.step is null when no STEP
             was created), metrics,
             params?, warnings?, script_output?,
             preview?, diff?, comparison_phases?, viewer?, viewer_glb?,
             viewer_opened?, project_viewer?, renders?, timings
             timings (ms): validation (pre-execution static script
               checks, not geometry), script_exec, metrics, export_step
               (umbrella) = source_validation + export_write + reload +
               delivered_validation, then optional preview/export/render
               phases and total. Stderr heartbeats carry the same phase
               names with elapsed seconds.
             project_viewer: url, latest_version, opened, reused; or
               status=unavailable and message if the service failed.
               latest_version is published and ready, not confirmation

Interrupted version recovery:
  agentcad context
    Read recovery.status and recovery.candidates. Context never repairs or
    changes version metadata/history.
    A candidate is recoverable only when output.step exists and there is
    no metadata or version-number conflict. Directories without a core STEP
    are reported but never deleted automatically.

  agentcad recover v3_edit
    Parse and validate v3_edit/output.step, compute fresh metrics, and
    restore missing meta.json and/or the manifest entry using an atomic JSON
    replacement for each file. Recovery is safely retryable if an I/O error
    occurs between those writes. Existing
    valid metadata fields are preserved. The recovered version is successful
    history, but current is unchanged by default. Optional artifacts left
    pending by the interruption become unavailable; recovery does not rerun
    post-processing.

  agentcad recover v3_edit --make-current
    Perform the same validation and explicitly advance current.

  Safety rules:
    - recovery never deletes or moves the directory, STEP, or source files;
    - malformed/invalid STEP is preserved and not registered as success;
    - corrupt metadata is preserved rather than overwritten;
    - duplicate version numbers stop with status=conflict;
    - recovery is explicit: context never repairs history by itself.

Daemon (auto-managed background worker):
  The first 'agentcad run' in a venv spawns a background daemon
  that keeps CadQuery/OCP loaded in memory. Subsequent heavy commands
  route through it without paying that parent-process import cost
  again; optional comparison workers still have their own cost.
  Each venv gets its own daemon (per-venv socket path). After a pip
  upgrade, a running daemon continues using the version loaded at
  startup. Routed commands and daemon status warn on a mismatch;
  run 'agentcad daemon restart' to load the installed version.

  Agents do not need to start, stop, or check the daemon. It just
  works. The commands below exist for diagnostics:

  Long routed commands send a progress heartbeat on stderr every few
  seconds while stdout stays reserved for the final JSON response.
  Each heartbeat keeps the submitted request attached beyond the
  30-second response-idle window; the command is never resubmitted.
  The final response includes via='daemon' and preserves the command's
  exit code. A completely silent/lost daemon exits 124 and returns
  error_kind='daemon_response_timeout' or 'daemon_response_lost',
  outcome='unknown', and retry_safe=false. Inspect project outputs,
  'agentcad context', and 'agentcad daemon status' before retrying so
  you do not duplicate side effects.

  agentcad daemon status  — Check if a daemon is running for this
                            venv; reports pid and version.
  agentcad daemon stop    — Force-stop the daemon (frees memory).
                            Next 'agentcad run' will spawn a new one.
  agentcad daemon restart — Reload the installed agentcad version
                            after an upgrade warning.

  COMMAND --no-daemon       — One-off opt-out for any daemon-routed
                              heavy command (does not spawn or route).

  Platform note (Windows):
    The daemon requires POSIX primitives (os.fork, AF_UNIX,
    os.getuid) and is disabled on Windows. Every command runs
    directly — output is identical to a POSIX run with --no-daemon,
    but each invocation pays the full OCP import cost (~seconds).
    'agentcad daemon' subcommands
    return {"status": "unsupported"} on Windows instead of
    attempting to spawn.

Feedback:
  agentcad feedback "your observation"

  Hit friction? Confused by an error? Wish a helper existed? Send it —
  any observation, mid-task, no permission needed. Your message is
  bundled with the recent session log and goes straight to the agentcad
  team. Casual, partial, just-a-thought messages are exactly the signal
  we want.

  --local-only     Save the bundle locally without sending.
  --max-entries N  Session log entries to include (default 10).

MCP integration — native agent tools:
  agentcad ships with an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so agents
  can call commands as native tools instead of shelling out to the CLI.

  Setup:
    1. Install the MCP extra:
       pip install agentcad[mcp]

    2. Add to your .mcp.json (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.):
       {"agentcad": {"command": "python", "args": ["-m", "agentcad.mcp"]}}

  Available tools:
    import_cad Import local STEP/STP/BREP with a default inspection bundle
    run       Execute a build123d script (or explicit CadQuery compatibility
              script), producing STEP + metrics
    render    Render PNG views of a STEP file
    export    Export STEP to mesh formats (stl, glb, obj)
    measure   Dimensional report (overall metrics and feature sizes)
    inspect   Topology report (solids, shells, faces, validity)
    check_spec Check a STEP against a JSON cylindrical-feature spec
    docs      Show documentation (this command)
    context   Project state plus interrupted-version recovery candidates
    recover   Validate and reconcile interrupted version history
    diff      Compare two versions
    view      Open GLB/STEP in browser

  Local CAD tools accept a 'cwd' parameter pointing to the project directory.
  Explicit cloud_* tools use hosted projects and optional local upload/
  download paths; see agentcad docs cloud for credentials and workflow.
  Responses are the same JSON as the CLI — same schema, same fields.
  import_cad(file, cwd, initialize=True) maps to import --init, using
  build123d by default. runtime can pin a newly initialized project only.
  build_dir selects the artifact root; view/diff match CLI controls.
  The default import response includes quality, dimensions, ID inventory
  references, and up to nine actual PNG attachments in inspection.media
  order. report=False omits inline inspection and attachments while
  retaining the saved bundle. report_images=False skips inspection
  media while keeping the report; max_images (0..9) caps media. These
  controls do not disable legacy import preview artifacts. text_budget
  bounds only the inspection object (default 2000 estimated tokens).
  An attachment failure leaves successful CAD import intact and reports
  image_delivery.status=failed, attached=0 and a retrieval action.
  file/cwd and artifact paths name the execution filesystem. PNGs are
  attached for the calling agent; use inspect for another ID or run
  for the edit.py scaffold. cloud_import instead uploads to a hosted
  project. Local import needs no cloud account. Unsupported import_cad
  arguments are rejected before work, rather than silently ignored.

  Why MCP over CLI?
    - No shell parsing — structured parameters in, structured JSON out.
    - Persistent process — the CAD runtime stays loaded between calls.
    - Native tool UI — agents see typed parameters, not raw argv.

Cloud projects through the CLI or local MCP server:
  Requires an API address and issued key pair from your host.
  Install pip install 'agentcad[cloud]' for the CLI, or 'agentcad[mcp]'
  for both CLI and native cloud tools. Start the usual local MCP server:
    python -m agentcad.mcp
  Set AGENTCAD_API_URL, AGENTCAD_KEY_ID, AGENTCAD_KEY_SECRET in that
  process environment (or your CLI shell). Keep secrets in a password
  manager, not project files, command arguments, or agent messages.
  API_URL must be an HTTPS origin; HTTP is allowed only on loopback
  for development. No login or local AgentCAD project is needed.

  Cloud tools are explicit and coexist with local tools:
    cloud_create_project(name, runtime='build123d'), cloud_projects(),
    cloud_project(project), cloud_run(project, script, label, cwd),
    cloud_import(project, file, cwd), cloud_measure(project, version),
    cloud_inspect(project, version),
    cloud_check_spec(project, version, spec_file, cwd),
    cloud_render(project, version),
    cloud_diff(project, from_version, to_version),
    cloud_job(project, job, wait_seconds=0), cloud_download(...).

  CLI examples (PROJECT/JOB are returned IDs):
    agentcad cloud projects create --name Bracket --runtime build123d
    agentcad cloud projects list
    agentcad cloud run PROJECT model.py --label first
    agentcad cloud job PROJECT JOB --wait
    agentcad cloud measure PROJECT 1
    agentcad cloud inspect PROJECT 1 --summary
    agentcad cloud check-spec PROJECT 1 spec.json
    agentcad cloud render PROJECT 1
    agentcad cloud diff PROJECT 1 2
    agentcad cloud download PROJECT part.step --job BUILD_JOB
    agentcad cloud import PROJECT part.step
    agentcad cloud download PROJECT iso.png --job RENDER_JOB --kind render
    agentcad cloud download PROJECT report.json --job CHECK_JOB --kind report
    agentcad cloud download PROJECT copy.step --version 1 --path v1_first/output.step

  Submission returns immediately with a job and idempotency_key. Keep
  that key for an identical lost-response retry using --idempotency-key
  or the MCP parameter. Never automatically resubmit a running job.
  cloud_job returns status plus nested result or measurement when done.
  Poll that same job; --wait defaults to 30 seconds, --wait-seconds and
  MCP wait_seconds allow at most 60 seconds of polling per call.
  For an edit, change the explicit local script, submit with a new key
  and label, then compare the returned cloud version numbers.

  Only named .py (256 KiB), STEP (20 MiB), or JSON spec (256 KiB) files
  are uploaded. Local-only run/render/measure options, dependency
  installation, directories, browser viewers, and folder sync are not
  cloud operations. The host uses its installed build123d/CadQuery stack.
  Missing files and unavailable packages are errors, not auto-installed.
  The cloud engine may differ from your locally installed version.

  Use project/version/path artifact references, not local paths or raw
  URLs, for later cloud tools. Downloads need an explicit destination
  in an existing directory; use --overwrite/overwrite=True explicitly
  to replace a file. Interrupted downloads publish no partial file.

  Command completion, geometry_valid, spec passed, and human review
  are separate. A completed failed spec has passed=false; unsupported
  requirements can leave passed=null. Preserve comparison_3d's exact/
  approximate method and unavailable/timeout states. Unavailable does
  not mean unchanged; rendering does not establish validity.
  This is a local MCP adapter calling HTTPS, not a hosted remote MCP URL.
  Full setup and build/edit walkthrough:
    https://github.com/jdilla1277/agentcad/blob/main/docs/cloud-workflow.md

Rendering:
  agentcad render <step_file> --view <spec> [--zoom N] [--size WxH] [--msaa N] [--name label] [--focus x,y,z] [--no-fit]

  --view   Named views (front, back, left, right, top, bottom, iso),
           comma-separated, 'all', custom 'azimuth:elevation', or a mix.
  --zoom   Zoom factor applied after FitAll (default 1.0).
  --size   Output resolution as WIDTHxHEIGHT (default 800x600).
  --msaa   Antialiasing samples, 0-16 (default 0). Nonzero values also
           use 2x supersampling to ensure offscreen antialiasing.
  --focus  Camera target point as 'x,y,z'.
  --no-fit Skip FitAll (requires --focus).
  --name   Custom filename for single-view renders.
  --highlight validation  Draw reported validation failures in red;
           writes to a validation/ subdirectory and includes the report.
  View/focus syntax, --no-fit's focus requirement, and --name's single-view
  requirement are checked before missing-path recovery, daemon routing,
  or CAD/renderer imports. Input errors return next_actions for help.
